summary: The ADR states intent clearly, but it cannot be implemented as written: it never defines the actual notice or a dependency license policy, so implementers cannot tell which files to stamp or which libraries are allowed.

questions.text: Which dependency license categories are allowed, need owner or legal sign-off, or are forbidden, and who resolves a flagged case?
questions.reason: Decides which libraries (MicroHs modules, JSON libs, web assets) can ship and how they may be linked; the ADR only says to identify license questions, resolve them explicitly and get legal review when unclear, with no criteria.

questions.text: What notice and ownership apply to SDK-generated or copied code that ends up in third-party plugin bundles?
questions.reason: Stamping proprietary headers on generated code inside third-party plugins conflicts with the extensibility goal; the ADR only says generated/copied code is in review scope and that the plugin boundary is independent of licensing.

questions.text: What is the exact Kyyn-owned notice (wording, copyright holder) and where does it go: per-file headers, repo-level file, embedded in artifacts, or a mix?
questions.reason: Decides whether every source file, one repo file, or the build pipeline changes; the ADR refers to 'the intended notice' and an 'all-rights-reserved notice' but never gives text, holder or placement.

questions.text: Should existing permissive LICENSE files or headers on Kyyn-authored prototypes be replaced, left alone, or flagged for an owner decision after provenance review?
questions.reason: Decides whether implementation includes a cross-repo migration or only an inventory; the ADR requires provenance review before changing repo license files and forbids silent rewrites, but not what the review should lead to.

questions.text: Is the pre-distribution notice and dependency check an automated build/CI gate or a manual release checklist?
questions.reason: A gate means SBOM/notice tooling with failure behaviour, a checklist means docs only; the ADR rules out only runtime enforcement ('one dependency-selection check').

questions.text: Under what terms do third-party plugin authors receive the proprietary SDK and plugin interfaces today?
questions.reason: Decides whether the SDK ships externally with a EULA/grant or stays internal this phase; the ADR forbids promising public redistribution rights and separates distribution permissions from extensibility, but grants nothing.

questions.text: How do third-party notices reach recipients inside distributed artifacts: an aggregated notices file, per-bundle notices, an about screen, or only the in-repo inventory?
questions.reason: Decides packaging work and whether the inventory must be machine-readable; the ADR says to preserve and retain required notices and points to vendor/README.md and dependency-sources.md, but not how notices travel.

questions.text: What counts as a 'distribution' that triggers the notice check: internal builds, tester builds, SDK releases, published plugins?
questions.reason: Decides which pipelines run the check; the ADR says 'for any distribution' without defining the term.
